children.translated_text: Now begins the <s>Yamasmṛti</s> (Laws of Yama).
Salutation to Lord <s>Gaṇeśa</s>.
Now, the description of expiations (<s>prāyaścitta</s>).
Now, therefore, of this <s>dharma</s> (law),
that which declares the expiations (<s>prāyaścitta</s>)
for all four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes),
the <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (law treatise) proceeds.
Those who have fallen [from their vows] through water, fire, hanging,
renunciation, fasting, or [other forms of] abandonment,
through poison, falling from heights, or expiation [attempts],
or those who have fallen through weapon-inflicted injuries —
all those who have [thus] settled [into sin],
excluded from all communities,
are purified by the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> [vow],
or by two <s>taptakṛcchra</s> (heated penance) observances.
Those sinful ones who are settled in both [categories],
who have fallen from shelter outside the village,
are purified by two lunar [months of penance],
and by giving a cow and a bull.
One who has burned [alive] a cow-slayer or Brahmin-slayer,
or [finds] one dead by hanging,
having cut the noose of that [person],
should perform the <s>taptakṛcchra</s> (heated penance).
One afflicted by worms born from wounds,
or struck by flies or horses,
should perform half a <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance),
and should give a gift (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) according to his ability.
When in the impure orifice of a Brahmin
pus and blood have arisen,
when worms have eaten the wound, [he is purified]
by a <s>homa</s> (fire oblation) with the <s>mauñjī</s> (muñja grass girdle).
A <s>kṣatriya</s>, a <s>vaiśya</s>,
or a <s>śūdra</s> born in legitimate order (<s>anuloma</s>),
who knowingly eats [forbidden food] in particular,
should observe the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow.
One should prepare each morsel
the size of a hen's egg.
Otherwise, due to the fault of [improper] food,
one is not purified thereby.
One should increase [morsels] by one each [day] during the bright fortnight,
and decrease them during the dark fortnight.
On the new moon (<s>amāvāsyā</s>), one should not eat —
this is the rule of the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s>.
For drinking liquor (<s>surā</s>) or other intoxicants,
or for eating cow's flesh,
a Brahmin should perform the <s>taptakṛcchra</s> (heated penance);
then that sin is destroyed.
If, when an expiation has been undertaken,
the performer perishes,
he is purified on that very day,
both in this world and the next.
As long as only one person with separate property
is purified by the expiation,
the others should not be touched;
they too are all condemned.
They are those whose food should not be eaten, whose gifts should not be accepted,
with whom one should not study together or contract marriage.
They are purified when the supplementary vow is completed;
all of them [then become] entitled to inheritance.
For one under eleven years of age
but above five years,
the expiation should be performed by the brother,
or the father, or another kinsman.
And for one younger than that,
there is neither offense nor sin.
The king's punishment does not apply to such a one,
nor is any expiation prescribed.
One who is eighty years old,
or a child under sixteen,
deserves half the expiation,
as do women and the sick.
When the sun has set,
[and one has been touched by] <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, washerman, or [their] women,
if one is touched by them at that time,
what should be the expiation?
Gold (<s>jātarūpa</s>) and refined gold (<s>suvarṇa</s>),
and water that was fetched during the day —
by bathing in and drinking that,
all of them are declared pure.
Servants, barbers, cowherds,
family friends, and sharecroppers —
these among the <s>śūdras</s> are those whose food may be eaten,
as well as one who has devoted himself [to a Brahmin].
Those ignorant men who eat
the food of a <s>śūdra</s> [other than these],
having thus incurred [sin],
should observe the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow.
When the twelfth year has arrived,
he who does not give [his] daughter [in marriage],
month after month, the menstrual blood —
the father [virtually] drinks that blood.
The mother, the father,
and the eldest brother likewise —
these three go to hell
upon seeing the maiden menstruating [unmarried].
The Brahmin who, deluded by pride,
marries such a maiden,
is one with whom one should not speak, unfit to sit in a row [at meals] —
that Brahmin is [called] a husband of a <s>vṛṣalī</s> (degraded woman).
A barren woman is to be known as a <s>vṛṣalī</s>;
a <s>vṛṣalī</s> is also one whose children have died.
A <s>śūdrī</s> (Śūdra woman) is to be known as a <s>vṛṣalī</s>,
as is an [unmarried] maiden who has menstruated.
Whatever [sin] a twice-born incurs by associating
with a <s>vṛṣalī</s> for one night,
that he removes by living on alms
and constantly reciting [mantras] for three years.
She who abandons her own husband [and goes]
to another man — [according to] <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
she is to be known as a <s>vṛṣalī</s>;
a <s>śūdrī</s> does not [thereby] become a <s>vṛṣalī</s>.
For one who has drunk the froth [of the lips] of a <s>vṛṣalī</s>,
or has been touched by her breath,
or for one begotten upon her —
no expiation whatsoever exists.
One afflicted with leucoderma or leprosy,
one with deformed nails, one with discolored teeth,
a diseased person, one with deficient or excess limbs,
a tale-bearer, and an envious person,
an unfortunate person, a eunuch (<s>ṣaṇḍa</s>),
a heretic (<s>pāṣaṇḍin</s>), one who reviles the <s>Vedas</s>,
a sophist (<s>haituka</s>), one who sacrifices for <s>śūdras</s>,
and one who sacrifices for those unworthy of sacrifice,
one constantly greedy for gifts,
a beggar, one attached to sense objects,
one with discolored teeth, a physician,
and one who speaks falsely,
these are to be carefully avoided
at <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) and gift-giving.
Also a temple priest (<s>devalaka</s>),
a hired [priest], one who sells the <s>Vedas</s>,
these are to be carefully avoided —
thus declared <s>Bhāsvat</s> (the Sun, i.e., Yama).
He who employs these persons
in rites for gods (<s>havya</s>) and ancestors (<s>kavya</s>),
his ancestors depart without hope,
going away [ignored] by gods and great sages.
Seeing a buffalo-keeper at the beginning [of the meal],
a husband of a <s>vṛṣalī</s> in the middle,
and a usurer at the end —
the ancestors depart without hope.
A '<s>mahiṣī</s>' (chief wife) is she who is called a wife
and who is adulterous.
He who tolerates those faults
is indeed known as a '<s>māhiṣika</s>' (buffalo-keeper, i.e., one who tolerates his wife's adultery).
One who collects [goods] of equal value
and sells them at a higher price,
he is indeed called a '<s>vārdhuṣika</s>' (usurer),
condemned among those who speak of <s>Brahman</s>.
As long as the food remains hot,
as long as they eat in silence,
the ancestors eat that long,
as long as the qualities of the oblation are not mentioned.
The qualities of the oblation should not be spoken of
where the ancestors have been satisfied.
After the ancestors are satisfied,
one may [then] speak [praising] the excellent oblation.
As many morsels as the mantra-knowing [Brahmin]
swallows at the rites for gods and ancestors,
that many rice-balls (<s>piṇḍas</s>)
the father of the Brahmin's body swallows.
A twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) who is touched by the leavings [of food]
or by one [contaminated] with leavings, or by a dog or <s>śūdra</s>,
by fasting for one night
is purified by the five cow-products (<s>pañcagavya</s>).
When touched by one who is not [contaminated] with leavings,
only bathing is prescribed.
But when touched by that same person [contaminated] with leavings,
one should perform the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [penance].
As long as Brahmins are not honored
with feasting and gold,
even for one who has completed his vow,
that sin does not perish.
When the body has been smeared by crow, crane, or kite droppings,
or has become soiled by impure substances,

children.translated_text: and it has entered [the skin] on the limbs or face properly —
purification from that soiling is by bathing.
Excluding the two hands, [if a part] above the navel
is contaminated,
above [the navel] — bathing; below — washing with water (<s>śauca</s>);
one is purified by that measure alone.
Regarding the eating of things not to be eaten,
things not to be drunk, things not to be licked,
and [the consumption of] semen, urine, and excrement —
what should be the expiation?
Lotus, <s>udumbara</s> (fig tree), <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple),
<s>kuśa</s> (sacred grass), <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), <s>palāśa</s> (flame tree) —
by drinking the water [infused with] these,
one is purified in six nights.
A Brahmin who has fallen [from his vows],
who has abandoned his [sacred] fires through renunciation without distress,
who was one without established fires and now resides [again],
and desires to take up the householder's life,
should perform three <s>kṛcchra</s> (penances)
and observe <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> [vows].
Through the prescribed rites beginning with the birth ceremony (<s>jātakarma</s>),
he deserves re-consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>).
Mattresses, pillows,
flowers, and red garments —
by drying them in heat
and sprinkling them, one becomes pure.
Considering the place, the time, oneself,
the substance, and the purpose of the substance,
the occasion and the circumstance,
one should practice <s>dharma</s> [accordingly].
Roads, muddy waters,
boats, metal [vessels], and grasses,
are purified by wind and sunlight,
as are [structures] built with fired bricks.
When a sick person [needs] a bath to be administered,
a healthy person [should bathe] ten times.
Having bathed repeatedly, one should touch that [sick person];
then the sick person is purified.
A washerman, a leather-worker,
an actor, and a <s>Buruḍa</s> (basket-maker),
a fisherman (<s>kaivarta</s>), a <s>Meda</s>, and a <s>Bhilla</s> —
these seven are known as outcaste (<s>antyaja</s>).
One who goes to the women of these
should perform the <s>taptakṛcchra</s> (heated penance).
Regarding women who are menstruating —
when touch or non-touch occurs,
what is the expiation for them,
prescribed for each <s>varṇa</s> (class)?
Having touched a menstruating woman
of the same <s>gotra</s> (lineage) and who has a husband,
whether intentionally or unintentionally,
one is purified by bathing at the [proper] time.
When a Brahmin woman and a <s>śūdra</s>-born woman
touch each other while menstruating,
the former is purified by a [full] <s>kṛcchra</s> penance;
the <s>śūdra</s> woman is purified by a quarter [of it].
When a <s>kṣatriya</s> woman and a <s>śūdra</s>-born woman
touch each other while menstruating,
the former should perform [a penance] reduced by a quarter;
the latter, half of a quarter.
When a <s>vaiśya</s>-born woman and a <s>śūdra</s>-born woman
touch each other while menstruating,
the former should perform a quarter <s>kṛcchra</s>;
the latter, half of that.
A menstruating woman who is touched
by dogs, goats, jackals, or donkeys —
she should remain fasting that long;
by bathing at the [proper] time, she is purified.
A non-menstruating woman touched
by <s>Caṇḍālas</s> while menstruating [is purified] —
by the <s>Prājāpatya kṛcchra</s> (penance)
and a hundred <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath controls).
A Brahmin who is touched at night
by a menstruating woman (<s>udakyā</s>) or by an outcast (<s>patita</s>),
should be bathed with water fetched during the day,
in the presence of fire.
During the day, [water is purified] by being touched by the sun's rays;
at night, by the rays of the stars.
At the twilight junctions of both [dawn and dusk],
water is always purifying.
Water touched by the tips of the nails of the hands —
a twice-born should drink [only such water] at the <s>ācamana</s> (sipping ritual).
Otherwise, he clearly drinks liquor (<s>surā</s>) —
such is the word of <s>Yama</s>.
In one's own well or reservoir or well,
by stones or by sharp instruments,
and by striking with a staff also
with a lump of earth or by a herd of cattle,
by obstruction, by binding,
by being placed [in danger], or by a basket (<s>puṣkala</s>),
by a piece of wood, by a tree, by an obstruction,
in a narrow passage, by ropes or cloth —
all this has been told to you,
the highest occasions of negligence.
Wherever cows have died,
one should perform an expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>).
For killing with wood, [one should perform] a <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance);
with stones, it should be double.
For [death in] a pit, a half-<s>kṛcchra</s>;
for [death by] a tree, a quarter-<s>kṛcchra</s>.
For killing with a weapon, three <s>kṛcchras</s>;
for killing with a stick, one should perform two.
By a <s>kṛcchra</s> even for killing with cloth,
a cow-killer is thus purified.
He who drives [cattle] in the midst of cows,
near a river or a dangerous pass —
in the first quarter [of the penance], the body hair [is shaved];
in the second, the beard should be shaved.
In the third, the topknot (<s>śikhā</s>) should be maintained;
in the fourth, [the head] should be shaved together with the topknot.
One should not perform the shaving of women;
nor should she follow the cow [in the vow].
Nor should she dwell in the cow-pen at night;
nor should she perform Vedic recitation.
Having pulled up all the hair,
one should cut two finger-widths.
Thus indeed for women,
this is considered the shaving of the head.
By [the presence of] a dead [child] or a newborn,
both [parents] incur birth-impurity (<s>sūtaka</s>).
But when smeared with sin (<s>pātaka</s>),
there is no birth-impurity for him.
Four activities indeed
one should avoid at twilight (<s>sandhyā</s>-time):
eating, sexual intercourse, sleep,
and Vedic study as the fourth.
From eating [at twilight], disease arises;
from intercourse, a cruel embryo.
From sleep, prosperity departs;
from Vedic study, death is certain.
O best of the twice-born, out of ignorance,
and desiring the welfare of the <s>varṇas</s> (social orders),
this scripture has been proclaimed by me —
listen attentively and understand.
Thus concludes the <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> spoken by <s>Yama</s>.
